title: Silk Film Culture System for in vitro Analysis and Biomaterial Design
protocol: Produce or purchase a desired topographic surface for casting.
Weigh out polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) potting and catalyst solution in a 1:9 ratio.
Mix solutions thoroughly to initiate curing process.
Place silicon wafer surface within a casting dish.
Weigh out 4.5 g of PDMS solution onto the silicon wafer.
Spread PDMS solution to cover a 100 mm diameter area on the wafer surface.
Tilt wafer to spread PDMS solution evenly.
Cover wafer with a 100 mm diameter petri dish lid.
Place casting setup into a 60 °C oven overnight, ensuring curing occurs on a flat surface.
Place cured PDMS/silicon wafer into a 70% ethanol bath before removal.
Begin removing PDMS from the wafer by using a razor blade to lift the edge (entire circumference) first.
Gently pull PDMS off using forceps within a 70% ethanol bath, being careful not to tear the silicone rubber casting.
Punch out individual PDMS molds using a 14 mm hole punch.
Bring 2 L of distilled water to a boil in a glass beaker.
Cut 5 g of Bombyx mori silkworm cocoons into thirds.
Measure 4.24 g of sodium carbonate.
Add sodium carbonate slowly to boiling dH2O, stirring until completely dissolved.
Boil cocoon pieces in dH2O for 40 min., stirring with a Teflon coated stir bar.
Drain boiling water and ring out silk extract by hand.
Wash silk extract three times for 20 min. each in 1 L of dH2O, using a stir bar to circulate the solution.
Ring out the washed silk extract by hand after each wash cycle.
Place washed silk fibers inside a chemical hood to dry for 12 hr.
Weigh dried silk fibers, typically ~3.5 g: ___________-g
Calculate necessary LiBr weight and volume for a 9.3 M solution of LiBr based on step 10's silk weight.
Add calculated LiBr weight into a glass beaker containing (0.8) x (calculated volume from step 11.a) mL of dH2O.
Pour the LiBr solution into an appropriate sized graduated cylinder and bring to final volume as determined in step 11.a.
Place dried silk fibers into a beaker and pour LiBr solution over them, ensuring all fibers are immersed.
Place the dissolved silk into an oven at 60 °C for 4 hours.
Using an appropriate sized syringe, draw up 12 mL of the silk solution.
Place an 18G needle on the end of the syringe and inject the solution into a dialysis cassette (3,500 MW cutoff, Slide-A-Lyzer, Thermo Scientific).
Draw out any remaining air from the cassette with the emptied syringe.
Place the filled dialysis cassette within 1 L of deionized water.
Change the deionized water volume after 1 hour, 4 hours, 8 hours, and then every 12 hours for a total of three changes at each interval.
Slowly collect the silk solution from the cassettes with syringe.
Place the collected solution into 10,000 g rated centrifuge tubes.
Centrifuge the solution twice at 10,000 g at 4 °C for 20 minutes each.
After each centrifugation, place the supernatant in a new tube.
Store the silk solution in a refrigerator at 4 °C.
Pipette two samples of 0.5 mL silk solution into small weigh dishes.
Place the weigh dishes inside a 60 °C dry oven for 12 hours or until the silk solution dries completely.
Weigh the remaining solid silk film from both samples to measure the silk solution percent weight-to-volume protein concentration.
Clean PDMS casting surfaces with clear tape to remove dust.
Soak PDMS substrates in 70% EtOH and wash three times with dH2O.
Place 14 mm PDMS molds onto a holder plate, typically a 24 well plate lid.
Spread 70 μL of an 8% silk solution on PDMS molds using a liquid spreading tool, typically a 1 mL syringe tip.
Dry the silk films uncovered on a clean bench with air flow pressure at 150 Pa for 90 min or until dry.
Place dried films into a water-annealing chamber with water in the bottom of an empty desiccator basin pulled at a 25 kPa vacuum for over 4 hours.
Remove silk films from the water-annealing chamber and place them onto a clean bench.
Sterilize control substrates, such as glass or plastic surfaces, by placing them into a 70% EtOH bath in a 35 mm Petri dish for at least 10 min.
Dip silk films removed from PDMS molds using forceps into 70% EtOH and place each sample into a well of a 24-well plate prefilled with 1 mL of 70% EtOH, ensuring the patterned side faces up.
Place stainless steel ring weights on top of each silk film in the wells.
Incubate samples with rings for 10 minutes to ensure sterility.
Remove EtOH from the samples.
Wash each sample three times with 1 mL of PBS.
Let each wash sit for 5 min to allow complete diffusion.
Remove PBS using an aspirating glass pipette, ensuring removal of most bubbles beneath silk film samples.
Trypsinize human corneal-limbal epithelial (HCLE) cell line with a 0.25% trypsin and EDTA solution for 7 minutes.
Deactivate trypsin by adding an equal volume of DMEM passage media containing 10% FBS.
Centrifuge the trypsinized HCLE cells.
Add 8 mL of keratinocyte-serum free media (K-SFM) to the cell pellet and gently agitate to disperse HCLEs.
Generate a cell count from the HCLE suspension.
Place 500 μL of HCLE suspension per well, typically using a density of 10,000 cells/cm².
Culture samples within an incubator at 37 °C with 5% CO₂ and proceed with the desired experimental protocol.
